facts.raw_span: A woman in her 40s presented with a 10-year history of progressive skin thickening and subcutaneous enlargement of the right side of her nose and right cheek
she had undergone nondiagnostic skin biopsies
she underwent a septorhinoplasty 6 months prior due to collapse of her right nasal ala
significant submucosal tissue was noted and removed from the right nasal cavity
enlargement of soft tissue with thickening of the overlying skin on her right cheek and right side of her nose several months later
slightly hyperplastic soft tissue with dilated patulous follicles involving the right medial malar cheek and right nasal ala
deviation of the nasal tip
fibroadipose tissue and vascular proliferation
sebaceous hyperplasia
subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells with varying density
thickened and fragmented collagen bundles
mature adipocytes extending into skeletal tissue

concepts.why: The patient's progressive skin thickening and subcutaneous enlargement, along with the presence of mature adipocytes extending into skeletal tissue, are consistent with Madelung's disease.
The patient's slightly hyperplastic soft tissue with dilated patulous follicles and subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells are consistent with nodular fasciitis.
The patient's significant submucosal tissue and mature adipocytes extending into skeletal tissue are consistent with lipomatosis of nerve.
The patient's deviation of the nasal tip and presence of fibroadipose tissue are consistent with fibrolipomatous hamartoma.
The patient's vascular proliferation and significant submucosal tissue are consistent with hemangioma.
The patient's progressive skin thickening and subcutaneous enlargement, along with the presence of mature adipocytes, are consistent with liposarcoma.
The patient's slightly hyperplastic soft tissue and subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells are consistent with fibromatosis.
The patient's significant submucosal tissue and vascular proliferation are consistent with angiolipoma.
